2.ja: 1914年8月4日、イギリスはドイツに宣戦し、遠距離封鎖に入った。グランド・フリートはオークニー諸島のスカパ・フローを根拠地に、スコットランドとノルウェーの間、北海の北の出口を押さえ、ドーヴァー海峡は別の部隊がふさいだ。ドイツの商船は、もう外洋に出られない。この封鎖は、ドイツ艦隊を撃滅しなくても、グランド・フリートが優勢を保って存在するだけで成り立った。
2.en: On 4 August 1914 Britain declared war on Germany, and the Royal Navy at once imposed a distant blockade. The Grand Fleet, based at Scapa Flow in the Orkneys, held the northern exit of the North Sea, between Scotland and Norway. A separate force closed the Strait of Dover. From then on, German merchant ships were shut out of the oceans. The blockade did not depend on destroying the German fleet. As long as the Grand Fleet existed, and stayed stronger, the blockade held.

3.ja: シェーアが5月末に予定した作戦は、巡洋戦艦でイギリス北東岸のサンダーランドを砲撃し、ロサイスの巡洋戦艦部隊をおびき出すものだった。大洋艦隊の主力は後方で待ち受け、ツェッペリン飛行船の偵察で、グランド・フリート主力が近くにいないことを確かめる。このため5月中旬から、イギリスの主な基地の沖に潜水艦を置き、出てくる艦を待ち伏せ、その動きを報告させた。
3.en: The German commander, Reinhard Scheer, planned a raid for the end of May 1916. His battlecruisers would shell Sunderland, on England's north-east coast, to draw the British Battlecruiser Fleet out of Rosyth, with the High Seas Fleet waiting behind them. Zeppelins would scout far ahead, to make sure the Grand Fleet itself was not at sea. From mid-May, U-boats took station off the main British bases, to attack ships coming out and report their movements.

4.ja: だが風向きが悪く、飛行船は飛べない。潜水艦も6月1日には引き揚げねばならない。シェーアは5月30日、予備の案に切り替えた。第1偵察群司令官フランツ・ヒッパー中将の巡洋戦艦が北上し、スカゲラク海峡の沖に姿を見せて、イギリスの哨戒部隊や商船を襲う。シェーアの主力は約50海里後ろに続く。前提は元の案と同じく、グランド・フリート主力の不在。それは作戦の前に崩れていた。
4.en: But for days the wind kept the airships grounded, and the U-boats could only stay on station until 1 June. So on 30 May Scheer switched to his fallback plan. Vice-Admiral Franz Hipper, commanding the 1st Scouting Group, would take the battlecruisers north and show himself off the Skagerrak, between Denmark and Norway, attacking British patrols and merchant ships there. The High Seas Fleet would follow about 50 miles behind. Like the first plan, it assumed the Grand Fleet would not be there. Before the operation even began, that was already untrue.

5.ja: ドイツ海軍の主力、大洋艦隊は、ヤーデ湾とヴィルヘルムスハーフェンを根拠地とした。開戦時の弩級主力艦はイギリスの約6割で、その差は縮まらなかった。そこでドイツ海軍は、グランド・フリート全体との決戦を避け、一部をおびき出してたたき、互角に近づいてから決戦を挑む方針をとった。1916年1月、病気のフォン・ポールに代わってラインハルト・シェーア中将が司令長官となり、方針の枠内でより積極的に動いた。4月24日から25日には、巡洋戦艦がイギリス東岸のローストフトとヤーマスを砲撃している。
5.en: The High Seas Fleet was the main force of the Imperial German Navy, based at Wilhelmshaven, on the Jade. In 1914 it had about six dreadnoughts for every ten British, and it never closed the gap. So German strategy was to avoid fighting the whole Grand Fleet: lure out part of it, destroy that part, and wear the British down until the two sides were nearly equal. Only then would they risk a decisive battle. In January 1916 Vice-Admiral Reinhard Scheer took over from the ailing Hugo von Pohl, determined to pursue that strategy far more actively. On 24 and 25 April his battlecruisers bombarded Lowestoft and Yarmouth, on England's east coast.

6.ja: 海軍省の暗号解読班は、旧庁舎の部屋番号から「40号室」と呼ばれた。ドイツ海軍の無線の大半を解読できた。5月30日、海軍省は大洋艦隊の翌日の出撃をつかみ、夕方グランド・フリートに出動を命じた。
6.en: The Admiralty's code-breakers worked in Room 40 of the Old Admiralty Building, and they became known simply as Room 40. They could read most German naval wireless traffic. On 30 May, intercepts showed that the High Seas Fleet would sail the next day, and that evening the Admiralty ordered the Grand Fleet to sea.

7.ja: 司令長官ジョン・ジェリコー大将は5月30日22時30分、スカパ・フローを出た。クロマーティの第2戦艦戦隊と、ロサイスの巡洋戦艦部隊も同時に出港した。
7.en: Admiral Sir John Jellicoe, commanding the Grand Fleet, sailed from Scapa Flow at 10:30 that night. At the same time, the 2nd Battle Squadron left Cromarty, and the Battlecruiser Fleet left Rosyth.

8.2.ja: 先行するのはデイヴィッド・ビーティー中将の巡洋戦艦部隊で、5月31日14時にユトランド半島西方の予定地点に着く。同じ時刻、ジェリコーの戦艦部隊はその北北西約69海里に着く。ビーティーは何も見つけなければ北へ転じて主力と合流し、全艦隊で捜索する手はずだった。
8.2.en: The plan was this. Vice-Admiral Sir David Beatty, commanding the Battlecruiser Fleet, would go on ahead, to reach a point west of the Jutland peninsula at 2 p.m. on 31 May. Jellicoe and the battle fleet would then be about 69 miles to the north-north-west. If Beatty had found nothing, he would turn north to join Jellicoe, and the whole fleet would sweep together.

9.ja: 基地沖のドイツ潜水艦は、イギリス主力艦に魚雷を1本も当てられず、その断片的な報告から、シェーアがグランド・フリートの全力出撃を知ることもなかった。イギリス側も途中で情報を誤る。12時30分、海軍省はジェリコーに、無線方位測定ではドイツ旗艦は11時10分にまだヤーデ湾にいる、と伝えた。
9.en: The U-boats waiting off the British bases failed to hit a single capital ship, and their scattered sighting reports never told Scheer that the whole Grand Fleet was out. But on the way, the British made an intelligence blunder of their own. At 12:30 p.m. on 31 May, the Admiralty told Jellicoe that, by wireless direction-finding, the German flagship had still been in the Jade at 11:10 that morning.

10.ja: ジェリコーは時間に余裕があると見て、駆逐艦の燃料を惜しんで増速せず、途中で中立国の船の臨検までした。その結果、主力の到着が遅れ、海軍省の情報への信頼も落ちた。後者は夜になって、もっと重く響く。
10.en: So Jellicoe thought he had time in hand. To save his destroyers' fuel he did not increase speed, and he stopped to examine neutral merchant ships on the way. It cost him in two ways. The battle fleet reached the scene later than it might have done. And Jellicoe's faith in Admiralty intelligence was shaken, which would matter far more that night.

11.ja: 実はシェーアは慣例どおり、旗艦のコールサインを陸上局に移し、別のコールサインで出港していた。作戦部長ジャクソン少将が40号室に尋ねたのは、そのコールサインの位置で、シェーアの居場所ではなかった。
11.en: What had really happened was routine. When Scheer put to sea, he handed his flagship's harbour call sign to a shore station and used another. The Director of Operations at the Admiralty, Rear-Admiral Thomas Jackson, had asked Room 40 where that call sign was, not where Scheer was.

12.ja: ヒッパーがヤーデ湾を出たのは5月31日1時、シェーアの主力は2時30分。先に海に出たのはイギリスだった。
12.en: Hipper left the Jade at 1 a.m. on 31 May, and Scheer's battle fleet followed at 2:30. The British had put to sea first.

13.ja: イギリスは151隻。弩級戦艦28、巡洋戦艦9、装甲巡洋艦8、軽巡洋艦26、駆逐艦78、機雷敷設艦と水上機母艦が各1隻。将兵約6万人。ドイツは99隻。弩級戦艦16、前弩級戦艦6、巡洋戦艦5、軽巡洋艦11、水雷艇61。ドイツでは、駆逐艦にあたる艦を大型水雷艇と呼んだ。将兵は約4万5千人。
13.en: The British brought 151 ships: 28 dreadnought battleships, 9 battlecruisers, 8 armoured cruisers, 26 light cruisers, 78 destroyers, a minelayer and a seaplane carrier, with some 60,000 men. The Germans brought 99: 16 dreadnoughts, 6 older pre-dreadnoughts, 5 battlecruisers, 11 light cruisers, and 61 torpedo boats, which was the German navy's name for its destroyers. They had about 45,000 men.

14.ja: 主砲はイギリスが12、13.5、15インチ、ドイツは11と12インチ。片舷斉射の砲弾重量では、イギリスがドイツの2倍を超えた。
14.en: The British capital ships carried 12-inch, 13.5-inch and 15-inch guns; the Germans, 11-inch and 12-inch. In weight of broadside, the British fired more than twice as much.

15.ja: 14時ごろ、両軍の前衛は50海里を切っていたが、互いに気づいていない。ビーティーは予定どおり北へ転じようとしていた。
15.en: By about 2 p.m. on 31 May, the two scouting forces were less than 50 miles apart, and neither knew it. Beatty was about to turn north, as planned.

16.ja: そのとき両軍の間に、デンマークの貨物船N・J・フィヨルド号が止まり、蒸気を噴いていた。ドイツ第2偵察群の軽巡洋艦エルビングが水雷艇2隻を臨検に出し、イギリス第1軽巡洋艦戦隊のガラティアも確かめに向かった。
16.en: Between them, a Danish steamer, the N. J. Fjord, had stopped and was blowing off steam. The German light cruiser Elbing, of the 2nd Scouting Group, sent two torpedo boats to inspect her. On the British side, Galatea, of the 1st Light Cruiser Squadron, came over to look as well.

17.ja: 14時20分、ガラティアは敵発見を信号し、28分に砲撃を始めた。
17.en: At 2:20, Galatea signalled that she had sighted the enemy. At 2:28 she opened fire.

18.ja: エルビングの応射の初弾がガラティアに当たったが、不発だった。
18.en: Elbing fired back, and scored the first hit of the battle, on Galatea. The shell failed to explode.

19.ja: 報告を受けたビーティーは14時32分、南南東へ転針した。ドイツ艦隊と基地の間に割り込み、退路を断つためだ。
19.en: At 2:32, on Galatea's report, Beatty turned south-south-east, to get between the Germans and their base and cut off their retreat.

25.ja: ここでこの日最初の通信の失敗が起きる。ビーティーの指揮下には巡洋戦艦6隻のほか、臨時に第5戦艦戦隊がいた。エヴァン＝トーマス少将のクイーン・エリザベス級4隻、バーラム、ヴァリアント、ウォースパイト、マラヤ。15インチ砲に24ノット、当時最強の主力艦である。
25.en: And here came the day's first signalling failure. Besides his six battlecruisers, Beatty had been lent the 5th Battle Squadron, under Rear-Admiral Hugh Evan-Thomas: four Queen Elizabeth-class battleships, Barham, Valiant, Warspite and Malaya. With 15-inch guns and a speed of 24 knots, they were the most powerful capital ships afloat.

25.5.ja: この戦隊は、ビーティーの旗艦ライオンの北西5海里にいた。転針命令は信号旗で出された。
25.5.en: They were five miles north-west of Beatty's flagship, Lion. Beatty ordered his turn by flag.

26.ja: 無線封止のためではない。ガラティアの発見報告は、すでに無線で送られていた。
26.en: Not for the sake of wireless silence. Contact had been made, and Galatea's report had gone out by wireless anyway.

26.5.ja: 当時、戦術運動の命令は信号旗が正式で、旗を降ろした瞬間に全艦が一斉に動ける。無線は暗号の処理に数分かかり、ふつうは状況報告や遠距離の連絡用だった。
26.5.en: In the Royal Navy of the day, flags were the proper way to order a manoeuvre. When the flags came down, the order was executed, and every ship moved at once. Wireless messages had to be coded and decoded, which took minutes, so they were used mainly for reports and long-distance traffic.

29.ja: 遠い艦には探照灯で繰り返すのが決まりだが、ライオンの信号員はそれをしなかった。中継役のタイガーも、隊形の変更で中継できる位置にいなかった。
29.en: When flags could not be read at that distance, the rule was to repeat them by searchlight. This time, Lion's signal staff did not. And Tiger, which was supposed to pass signals on, was no longer in position after a change of formation.

31.ja: バーラムからは遠いうえ煤煙に遮られ、旗が読めなかった。
31.en: In Barham, far off and with coal smoke in the way, nobody could read the flags.

35.ja: エヴァン＝トーマスは指揮下に入ってまだ数日で、信号がなくても旗艦に続け、という常設命令も受けていない。巡洋戦艦の転針は見えたが命令はなく、数分間、元の針路を進んだ。
35.en: Evan-Thomas had been under Beatty for only a few days. He had never been given the Battlecruiser Fleet's standing order: when the flagship turns, follow, even without a signal. He saw the battlecruisers turn, but no order reached him, so he held his course for several minutes.

38.ja: 転針して追ったときには約10海里遅れ、ビーティーは減速して待たなかった。こうして砲戦の最初の20分、イギリス最強の4隻は戦いに加われなかった。
38.en: By the time his squadron turned to follow, it was about ten miles astern. Beatty did not slow down to let it catch up. So for the first twenty minutes of the battlecruiser action, the four most powerful British ships took no part.

53.ja: 15時8分、水上機母艦エンガディンがショート184型水上機を発進させた。操縦はラトランド大尉。雲が約300メートルと低く、約270メートルを飛ぶしかなかった。
53.en: At 3:08, the seaplane carrier Engadine launched a Short 184 seaplane, flown by Flight Lieutenant Frederick Rutland. The cloud base was only about 1,000 feet, so he had to fly at around 900.

56.5.ja: ラトランドはドイツ軽巡洋艦を見つけて無線で報告したが、母艦エンガディンはそれをライオンに伝えられなかった。艦載機が海戦で敵艦隊を偵察した最初の例だが、役には立たなかった。
56.5.en: Rutland found the German light cruisers and reported them by wireless, but Engadine could not get the message through to Lion. It was the first time a ship-launched aircraft had scouted an enemy fleet in battle, and it made no difference at all.

61.ja: ドイツの弱みは数、強みは防御だった。主力艦の装甲は厚く、水密区画も細かい。15時20分ごろ、ヒッパーとビーティーの巡洋戦艦が互いを発見し、15時33分、ヒッパーは南東へ反転した。退却ではない。計画どおり、ビーティーを南方約50海里の大洋艦隊主力へ引き込むためだ。
61.en: The German fleet was weaker in numbers, but its ships were better protected, with thicker armour and finer watertight subdivision. At about 3:20, Hipper's and Beatty's battlecruisers sighted each other. At 3:33 Hipper turned south-east. He was not running away. He was drawing Beatty on, towards the High Seas Fleet, about 50 miles to the south.

85.ja: イギリスの13.5インチ砲は射程でまさっていたが、ビーティーはそれを生かさず、互いに届く距離まで近づいてから撃った。
85.en: Beatty's 13.5-inch guns outranged the German guns, but he threw that advantage away. He held his fire until he had closed to a range where both sides could hit.

93.ja: 15時48分、両軍の巡洋戦艦がほぼ同時に砲火を開いた。距離約1万5千ヤード、14キロほど。イギリスは先頭からライオン、プリンセス・ロイヤル、クイーン・メアリー、タイガー、ニュージーランド、インディファティガブルの6隻。ドイツはリュッツォウ、デアフリンガー、ザイドリッツ、モルトケ、フォン・デア・タンの5隻。両隊は並んで南へ走った。イギリスでいう「南への疾走」である。
93.en: At 3:48, the two lines of battlecruisers opened fire almost together, at about 16,000 yards. Beatty had six: Lion, Princess Royal, Queen Mary, Tiger, New Zealand and Indefatigable. Hipper had five: Lutzow, Derfflinger, Seydlitz, Moltke and Von der Tann. The two lines ran south on roughly parallel courses. This was the run to the south.

97.ja: 初めは見通しがドイツに有利だった。西のイギリス艦は明るい空を背にくっきり見え、東のドイツ艦の背後は灰色のもや。西風が煤煙と砲煙を両隊の間に流し、イギリス自身の観測を妨げた。
97.en: At first the light favoured the Germans. The British, to the west, stood out sharply against the bright western sky. The Germans, to the east, were set against a grey haze. And a westerly wind carried the British funnel and gun smoke between the lines, blinding their own spotters.

100.ja: ドイツのステレオ式測距儀は、砲戦初めの測距が速かった。数分でライオン、プリンセス・ロイヤル、タイガーが次々に被弾したが、イギリスの砲弾はまだ大きく外れていた。
100.en: The German stereoscopic rangefinders found the range faster. Within minutes Lion, Princess Royal and Tiger had all been hit, while the British shells were still falling well off target.

103.5.ja: 目標の割り振りでも誤りが出た。ビーティーの信号では、先頭2隻がドイツの先頭艦を撃ち、残りは順に1隻ずつ受け持つ。だが信号が正しく伝わらず、クイーン・メアリーはザイドリッツを撃ち、2番艦デアフリンガーは10分近く誰にも撃たれずに、落ち着いて狙いを定めた。
103.5.en: The British also mixed up their targets. Beatty's signal had his two leading ships concentrate on the leading German ship, and each of the others take its opposite number. But not every ship read it correctly. Queen Mary fired at Seydlitz, and the second German ship, Derfflinger, went unengaged for nearly ten minutes, free to aim in peace.

105.ja: 16時ちょうど、リュッツォウの1発がライオン中央のQ砲塔を貫き、砲塔員の大半が死傷した。砲塔長の海兵隊少佐ハーヴェイは両脚に重傷を負いながら、弾薬庫の扉を閉めて注水せよと命じた。
105.en: At 4 p.m., a shell from Lutzow burst inside Lion's Q turret, amidships, killing or wounding most of its crew. The turret commander, Major Francis Harvey of the Royal Marines, both legs shattered, still ordered the magazine doors shut and the magazine flooded.

108.ja: 約20分後、砲塔に残った装薬が燃え、炎はマストを越えたが、弾薬庫はすでに水の中で、ライオンは救われた。ハーヴェイは戦死し、ヴィクトリア十字章を追贈された。
108.en: Nearly half an hour later, the cordite left in the turret caught fire, and the flames shot higher than the mastheads. But the magazine was already flooded, and Lion survived. Harvey died of his wounds, and was awarded a posthumous Victoria Cross.

110.ja: 16時2分、最後尾のインディファティガブルがフォン・デア・タンの連続命中を受け、弾薬庫が爆発して数分で沈んだ。1019人中1017人が戦死。
110.en: At 4:02, Indefatigable, at the rear of the line, was hit again and again by Von der Tann. Her magazine exploded, and within minutes she was gone. 1,017 of her 1,019 men were killed.

113.ja: 16時8分、第5戦艦戦隊がようやく射程の限界に追いつき、約1万9千ヤード、17キロほどからドイツの後尾を撃ち始めた。フォン・デア・タンとモルトケが被弾し、フォン・デア・タンは約600トン浸水した。
113.en: At 4:08, the 5th Battle Squadron finally came within range, near its limit, and opened fire on the rear of the German line at about 19,000 yards. Von der Tann and Moltke were both hit, and Von der Tann took in some 600 tons of water.

131.ja: 16時26分、クイーン・メアリーがデアフリンガーとザイドリッツの集中射撃を浴び、前部弾薬庫が爆発。船体が折れて沈み、1266人が戦死した。
131.en: At 4:26, Queen Mary came under the combined fire of Derfflinger and Seydlitz. Her forward magazine blew up, her hull broke apart, and 1,266 men died.

134.ja: ビーティーは艦長に言った。「今日はどうも、いまいましい艦がどこかおかしいらしい」
134.en: On Lion's bridge, Beatty turned to his flag captain: "There seems to be something wrong with our bloody ships today."

136.ja: これより前、クイーン・メアリーの砲弾がザイドリッツの砲塔に命中して装薬が燃えたが、火は弾薬庫に届かなかった。同じ命中で結果が分かれたのは、装甲の厚さより、装薬の扱いの違いによる。
136.en: Earlier, Queen Mary had hit one of Seydlitz's turrets. The propellant inside caught fire, but the fire never reached the magazine. The same kind of hit had very different results on the two sides. The reason was how they handled their propellant, not simply how thick their armour was.

136.3.ja: 1914年8月28日のヘルゴラント・バイト海戦も、1915年1月24日のドッガー・バンク海戦も、前衛同士の戦いでドイツが敗れ、皇帝ヴィルヘルム2世は艦隊の行動をさらに縛った。
136.3.en: There had been two earlier clashes: Heligoland Bight, on 28 August 1914, and Dogger Bank, on 24 January 1915. Neither involved the main battle fleets, and the Germans lost both. Afterwards the Kaiser kept his fleet on an even tighter leash.

136.6.ja: ドッガー・バンクでは、ザイドリッツの後部砲塔に被弾して装薬が燃え、砲塔2基の乗員が全滅した。弾薬庫は注水が間に合って助かった。ドイツ海軍はこれに学び、弾薬の運び方と防火を改めた。
136.6.en: At Dogger Bank, a shell hit one of Seydlitz's after turrets and set the propellant alight. Everyone in both after turrets was killed, but prompt flooding saved the magazine. The German navy learned from it, and changed the way it handled ammunition and guarded against flash.

137.2.ja: イギリスには同じ経験がなく、改善もなかった。
137.2.en: The Royal Navy had no such warning, and changed nothing.

138.ja: 16時15分ごろ、両軍の駆逐艦と水雷艇が主力の間で戦い始めた。どちらも中間の海を抜けて敵主力を雷撃しようとし、途中でぶつかって近距離の乱戦になった。
138.en: At about 4:15, the destroyers and torpedo boats of both sides clashed between the battle lines. Each side was trying to cross the gap and torpedo the enemy's big ships. They met in the middle, in a close-range melee.

139.5.ja: ドイツ水雷艇V27とV29が沈んだ。
139.5.en: The German torpedo boats V27 and V29 were sunk.

145.ja: 16時33分、ビーティーの前方を偵察していた第2軽巡洋艦戦隊の旗艦サウサンプトンが、南東に多数の戦艦を発見した。グッドイナフ准将は16時38分、「敵戦艦部隊発見」と報告した。
145.en: At 4:33, Southampton, flagship of the 2nd Light Cruiser Squadron, scouting ahead of Beatty, sighted a mass of battleships to the south-east. At 4:38 Commodore William Goodenough sent his report: enemy battle fleet in sight.

149.ja: 彼はすぐには退かず、約12キロまで迫って数と隊形と針路を確かめてから反転した。その間、ドイツ戦艦の砲撃を浴び続けた。
149.en: He did not turn away at once. He kept closing, to about 13,000 yards, under fire from the German battleships the whole time, and turned only when he had their numbers, formation and course.

150.ja: 以後数時間、サウサンプトンは接触を保って報告を送り続けた。この海戦でイギリスが得た最良の偵察報告である。
150.en: For hours afterwards, Southampton kept in touch and kept reporting. Hers were the best scouting reports the British made in the whole battle.

151.ja: 南への疾走は16時40分に終わった。イギリスは巡洋戦艦2隻を失い、戦死2283人。ドイツは大型艦を失っていない。戦後の集計で、主砲弾の命中は、ドイツ巡洋戦艦が約42発、イギリス巡洋戦艦が約11発だった。
151.en: The run to the south ended at 4:40. The British had lost two battlecruisers and 2,283 men; the Germans had lost no big ship. Post-war counts give about 42 heavy-shell hits by the German battlecruisers, against about 11 by the British.

153.ja: 16時40分、ビーティーは北へ転じた。今度は彼が、シェーアとヒッパーをジェリコーの主力へ引き込む番だった。
153.en: At 4:40, Beatty turned north. Now the roles were reversed. It was Beatty's job to draw Scheer and Hipper north, onto the Grand Fleet.

154.ja: ジェリコーが出ていると知らないシェーアは、相手をビーティーだけと見て全速追撃を命じた。イギリスでいう「北への疾走」である。
154.en: Scheer did not know Jellicoe was at sea. He thought he faced only Beatty, and ordered a general chase at full speed. This was the run to the north.

155.5.ja: 第5戦艦戦隊はまた命令の伝達が遅れ、北へ戻る巡洋戦艦と反対向きにすれ違いながら、なお南へ進んだ。
155.5.en: And once again the 5th Battle Squadron's orders came late. When Beatty turned, Evan-Thomas was still heading south, and passed the battlecruisers going the other way.

162.ja: 16時57分、駆逐艦ペタードの魚雷がザイドリッツの艦首に命中したが、ザイドリッツは浸水しつつも速力を保ち、隊列にとどまった。
162.en: At 4:57, a torpedo from the British destroyer Petard hit Seydlitz forward. She took on water, but kept her speed and her place in the line.

168.ja: 反転の信号旗が降ろされたのは数分後で、戦隊はドイツ主力の方へ数海里よけいに進んだ。しかも反転は同じ地点で順に回る逐次回頭で、ドイツ戦艦はその一点に砲火を集中できた。
168.en: The flag signal to turn was hauled down several minutes late, so the squadron ran on several miles closer to the German battle fleet. And it turned in succession, each ship at the same spot, so the German battleships simply aimed at that spot.

168.6.ja: バーラムとマラヤが被弾。マラヤは副砲の装薬が燃えて100人以上が死傷したが、艦は救われた。
168.6.en: Barham and Malaya were both hit. In Malaya, cordite caught fire in a six-inch casemate, causing more than a hundred casualties, but her crew saved the ship.

169.ja: それから1時間あまり北への追撃が続く。ビーティーの巡洋戦艦は増速して一時接触を失い、しんがりの第5戦艦戦隊が4隻で、ヒッパーの巡洋戦艦5隻とドイツ第3戦艦戦隊の先頭の艦を相手にした。
169.en: For more than an hour, the chase went north. Beatty's battlecruisers drew ahead, and for a time lost touch altogether. The 5th Battle Squadron covered the rear: four battleships against Hipper's five battlecruisers and the leading ships of the German 3rd Battle Squadron.

170.ja: 第5戦艦戦隊は何度も被弾したが主装甲は破られず、脱落艦もない。逆にリュッツォウ、デアフリンガー、ザイドリッツなどに命中弾を重ねた。
170.en: Evan-Thomas's ships were hit many times, but their main armour was never pierced, and not one left the line. And they hit back, again and again, on Lutzow, Derfflinger, Seydlitz and others.

170.5.ja: 17時30分を過ぎると、ヒッパーの各艦はかなり傷んでいた。
170.5.en: By soon after 5:30, Hipper's ships were badly knocked about.

172.ja: このころ光の条件が変わる。太陽は西に低く、イギリス艦は北西。ドイツの測距員は太陽に向かって測ることになり、目標は光るもやに溶けた。逆にドイツ艦の輪郭は、イギリス側からよく見えた。
172.en: Now the light changed. The sun was low in the west, and the British were to the north-west. The German rangetakers were looking into the sun, at targets lost in a glowing haze, while the German ships stood out clearly to the British.

176.ja: シェーアはついにグランド・フリート主力に気づかなかった。理由は3つ。基地沖の潜水艦は役立つ情報を送らず、飛行船は低い雲と霧で何も見えず、前衛の偵察部隊は最後に持ち場から押しのけられた。
176.en: Scheer never found the Grand Fleet, for three reasons. The U-boats off the British bases told him nothing useful. The Zeppelins that went up that day saw nothing through the low cloud and haze. And at the last, his scouting forces were pushed away from where they should have been.

178.ja: 最後の点には2つの要因がある。ビーティーが17時35分から北東、さらに東へ回り込み、ヒッパーを東へ押しやったこと。そしてジェリコーが16時5分、フッド少将の第3巡洋戦艦戦隊、インヴィンシブル、インフレキシブル、インドミタブルを先に南へ急がせていたことだ。この3隻が北東から現れた。
178.en: That last was down to two things. First, from 5:35 Beatty bent his course round to the north-east, then east, forcing Hipper to give way eastwards. Second, at 4:05 Jellicoe had sent Rear-Admiral Horace Hood on ahead with the 3rd Battlecruiser Squadron, Invincible, Inflexible and Indomitable, to reinforce Beatty. Hood came onto the scene from the north-east.

198.ja: 駆逐艦ノーマッドとネスターは被弾して動けなくなり、やがて通りかかったドイツ戦艦に沈められた。
198.en: The British destroyers Nomad and Nestor were hit and stopped. Later, the German battleships came past and sank them.

201.ja: 17時36分、フッドの前方を偵察していた軽巡洋艦チェスターが、霧の中でベーディッカー少将のドイツ第2偵察群、軽巡洋艦4隻と遭遇し、数分で17発を浴びて大きな損害を出した。
201.en: At 5:36, the light cruiser Chester, scouting for Hood, ran into four German light cruisers in the haze: the 2nd Scouting Group, under Rear-Admiral Friedrich Bodicker. Within minutes she was hit seventeen times, with heavy casualties.

204.ja: 16歳の少年水兵ジャック・コーンウェルは致命傷を負っても砲を離れず、のちにヴィクトリア十字章を追贈された。
204.en: One of her gun crew, sixteen-year-old Boy First Class Jack Cornwell, stayed at his post though mortally wounded. He was awarded a posthumous Victoria Cross.

221.2.ja: 17時55分、フッドの3隻が砲撃を始め、ドイツ軽巡洋艦ヴィースバーデンは機関室に被弾して、両軍の間で止まった。
221.2.en: At 5:55, Hood's three battlecruisers came up and opened fire. The German light cruiser Wiesbaden was hit in the engine room, and left dead in the water between the fleets.

222.4.ja: ドイツ水雷艇がフッドの戦隊を雷撃し、イギリス駆逐艦シャークが阻止に出た。シャークは集中射撃で戦闘力を失い、19時ごろ沈没。艦長ジョーンズ中佐は戦死し、ヴィクトリア十字章を追贈された。
222.4.en: German torpedo boats attacked Hood's squadron. The British destroyer Shark went in to stop them. She was crippled by concentrated fire, and sank at about 7 p.m. Her captain, Commander Loftus Jones, was killed, and awarded a posthumous Victoria Cross.

223.5.ja: ヒッパーは東に主力艦の砲火を見てイギリス主力の到着と判断し、シェーアの戦艦部隊へ後退した。これでドイツ艦隊の前に偵察部隊はいなくなり、シェーアは前方の敵を知らないまま北上を続けた。
223.5.en: Hipper saw heavy gunfire to the east. Taking it for the British battle fleet, he fell back on Scheer's battleships. Now nothing was scouting ahead of the German fleet. Scheer was steaming north blind.

229.5.ja: ジェリコーの主力は北西から近づいていた。
229.5.en: Jellicoe and the battle fleet were coming down from the north-west.

230.3.ja: 戦艦24隻は4隻ずつ6列の縦隊で、横に並んで進んでいた。航行や運動には便利だが、撃てるのは各列の前の艦だけだ。
230.3.en: His 24 battleships were in six columns of four, side by side. That formation was easy to steer and manoeuvre, but only the ships at the head of each column could fire.

232.ja: 戦うには1本の単縦陣に展開し、全艦の主砲を片舷に向ける必要がある。展開には約20分。どちら側に展開するかは敵の方位で決まるが、ジェリコーにはそれが分からなかった。
232.en: Before a battle, the fleet had to deploy into a single line, so that every big gun could bear on one side. Deployment took about twenty minutes, and which way to deploy depended on where the enemy was. Jellicoe did not know exactly where that was.

234.ja: 各艦の報告位置は推測航法の誤差で食い違い、ビーティーとジェリコーの間でも数海里ずれていた。
234.en: Ships' reported positions disagreed, because of errors in dead reckoning. Beatty's and Jellicoe's reckoned positions were several miles apart.

236.ja: 18時1分、ライオンを視認したジェリコーは「敵戦艦部隊はどこか」と問うた。使える答えは18時14分、「敵戦艦部隊、南南西」。両軍の主力は、もう10海里を切っていた。
236.en: At 6:01, Jellicoe sighted Lion and signalled: "Where is the enemy's battle fleet?" Not until 6:14 did he get a usable answer: south-south-west. By then the two battle fleets were less than ten miles apart.

240.ja: 選択肢は2つ。右翼の列を軸に展開すれば敵に近く、すぐ戦える。だが展開中、右翼の艦だけがドイツ戦列全体の砲火を浴び、水雷艇の射程にも入る。
240.en: He had two choices. Deploying on the starboard column, the one nearest the enemy, would bring him into action at once. But while the rest formed up, that column would take the fire of the whole German line alone, within reach of the German torpedo boats.

241.ja: 左翼の列を軸にすれば敵からは遠い。だが展開を終えると、イギリスの戦列はドイツ艦隊の行く手をふさぎ、敵と基地の間に入る。しかもイギリス艦は暗い東、ドイツ艦は明るい西に立つ。
241.en: Deploying on the port column would put him farther from the enemy. But once formed, the British line would lie right across the German course, and between the Germans and home. And the British would be in the darker east, the Germans against the brighter western sky.

241.5.ja: 18時15分、ジェリコーは左翼を軸とする展開を命じた。針路は南東から少し東寄り。6列の縦隊は長さ約6海里の1本の戦列になった。後の研究者の多くは、この判断を正しかったと見る。
241.5.en: At 6:15, Jellicoe ordered deployment on the port column, course south-east by east. The six columns unrolled into a single battle line about six miles long. Most historians since have judged it the right decision.

242.2.ja: 展開中、戦場の北側はひどく混み合った。ビーティーの巡洋戦艦は戦艦部隊の前を横切って先頭へ、第5戦艦戦隊は最後尾へ。巡洋艦や駆逐艦の隊がその間を縫い、航路が入り乱れた。すべてがドイツ艦の砲火の下だった。
242.2.en: While the fleet deployed, the northern end of the battlefield was badly congested. Beatty's battlecruisers had to cross ahead of the battle fleet to reach the head of the line, the 5th Battle Squadron had to fall in at the rear, and cruisers and destroyers were weaving through the gaps. Their tracks crossed, all under German fire.

242.6.ja: 将兵はのちにここを「ウィンディ・コーナー」と呼ぶ。ここで事件が重なった。
242.6.en: British sailors later called the spot Windy Corner. Several things happened there.

244.9.ja: 第1巡洋艦戦隊のアーバスノット少将は、装甲巡洋艦ディフェンスとウォリアーを率いて飛び出し、止まったヴィースバーデンを沈めようと、ドイツ主力から約7千ヤードまで迫った。18時20分、ディフェンスは戦艦と巡洋戦艦の集中射撃を浴びて弾薬庫が爆発し、903人全員が戦死した。
244.9.en: Rear-Admiral Sir Robert Arbuthnot, commanding the 1st Cruiser Squadron, charged out with the armoured cruisers Defence and Warrior to finish off the crippled Wiesbaden. He got within about 7,000 yards of the German heavy ships. At 6:20, Defence was caught by the fire of German battleships and battlecruisers. Her magazines blew up, and all 903 men aboard were killed.

246.6.ja: ウォリアーも大破し、翌朝、曳航中に沈んだ。
246.6.en: Warrior was badly damaged, and sank under tow the next morning.

247.5.ja: ウォースパイトは舵が故障し、ドイツ戦艦の射程内で2度旋回した。主砲弾13発を受けたが沈まず、のちに単独で帰投を命じられた。
247.5.en: In the 5th Battle Squadron, Warspite's steering jammed. She circled twice under the German battleships' guns and took thirteen heavy shells, but stayed afloat, and was later ordered home on her own.

251.ja: ドイツ艦隊は単縦陣で北東へ進み、その先頭がイギリス戦列の弧の中へ入りつつあった。いわゆるT字戦法の形だ。横棒の側は片舷の全砲火を使えるが、縦棒の側で応射できるのは先頭の数隻しかない。
251.en: The German fleet was steaming north-east in a single line, its head running into the arc of the British line. This is what sailors call crossing the T. The fleet forming the bar of the T can fire full broadsides; the fleet forming the stem can answer only with its leading ships.

255.ja: 18時30分ごろ、イギリスの戦列が次々に砲火を開いた。ドイツ側からは北から東の水平線に砲口の閃光が連なるだけで、艦影は見えない。第3戦艦戦隊の旗艦ケーニヒと、巡洋戦艦リュッツォウが続けて被弾した。
255.en: From about 6:30, the British battle line opened fire, ship after ship. To the Germans, the horizon from north to east was a continuous ripple of gun flashes, with no ships to be seen. Konig, flagship of the German 3rd Battle Squadron, and the battlecruiser Lutzow were hit again and again.

258.ja: 18時34分、もやが一瞬晴れた隙に、デアフリンガーとリュッツォウがフッドの旗艦インヴィンシブルをとらえた。中央の砲塔が貫かれて弾薬庫が爆発し、船体は二つに折れた。
258.en: At 6:34, in a brief break in the haze, Derfflinger and Lutzow found Hood's flagship, Invincible. A shell pierced her midships turret, her magazine blew up, and she broke in two.

259.ja: フッド以下1026人が戦死し、生存者は6人。この日3隻目の巡洋戦艦の喪失で、原因も前の2隻と同じだった。
259.en: 1,026 men died, Hood among them. Six survived. She was the third British battlecruiser lost that day, and she went the same way as the other two.

261.ja: シェーアはここで初めて、相手がグランド・フリート全体だと知った。18時33分、一斉回頭を命令。最後尾から順に、ほぼ同時に、全艦が右へ180度回る。
261.en: Only now did Scheer realise he was facing the whole Grand Fleet. At 6:33 he ordered a battle turn-away. Starting from the rear, each ship turned 180 degrees to starboard as soon as the ship astern of her began, so the whole line reversed almost at once.

262.6.ja: 劣勢から離脱するため、大洋艦隊が訓練を重ねた運動だ。
262.6.en: The High Seas Fleet had practised this manoeuvre specially, as a way to break off a fight it was losing.

263.5.ja: 数分でドイツ戦列は南西に向き、水雷艇の煙幕に隠れて霧に消えた。
263.5.en: Within minutes the whole German line had reversed to the south-west and vanished into the haze, behind smoke laid by the torpedo boats.

265.ja: ジェリコーは追わなかった。1914年に海軍省へ示した原則がある。退く敵を追えば魚雷や機雷を浴び、潜水艦の待ち伏せに誘い込まれかねない。彼は南東、続いて南へ向かい、ドイツ艦隊と基地の間を保った。
265.en: Jellicoe did not follow. He had set out his reasons to the Admiralty back in 1914: a fleet that chases a retreating enemy runs into torpedoes and mines dropped in its path, and may be led over a submarine ambush. Instead he turned south-east, then south, keeping between the Germans and their base.

279.5.ja: 18時54分、戦艦マールバラが魚雷を受けたが、隊列にとどまった。
279.5.en: At 6:54, the battleship Marlborough was hit by a torpedo, but kept her place in the line.

283.ja: 18時55分、シェーアは再び一斉回頭し、東へ引き返した。その意図は今もはっきりしない。
283.en: At 6:55, Scheer turned his whole fleet about again, back to the east. Why he did so has never been settled.

285.ja: シェーアは戦後の報告や回想録でこう説明した。まだ明るいうちに西へ退けば夕方じゅう追われる。反転して出れば敵の不意を突き、態勢を崩し、ヴィースバーデンも救える、と。
285.en: In his report and his memoirs, Scheer said it was still too early in the evening: if he went west now, the British would chase him until dark. Turning back would surprise them, upset their dispositions, and might let him rescue Wiesbaden.

286.5.ja: 多くの研究者は納得していない。英艦隊の位置を読み違え、その後ろを抜けるつもりが、戦列の中央へ向かってしまったと見る。
286.5.en: Many historians don't believe him. They think he misjudged where the British were, meant to pass astern of their line, and instead ran straight into its centre.

289.ja: 19時10分ごろ、ドイツの先頭は再びイギリス戦列の弧に入った。条件は1度目より悪い。西のドイツ艦は夕焼けを背に浮かび、東のイギリス艦は暗いもやの中。ドイツ側は砲口の閃光を狙うしかなかった。
289.en: At about 7:10, the head of the German line ran into the arc of British fire again, and this time it was worse. The Germans were in the west, outlined against the sunset. The British were in the east, in the gloom and haze, and the Germans could aim only at their gun flashes.

293.ja: 10分あまりで、ケーニヒ、グローサー・クルフュルスト、マルクグラーフ、カイザー、ヘルゴラントなどが被弾し、ドイツ艦の被弾は30発を超えた。イギリスはコロッサスの2発だけ。シェーアは3度目の反転を強いられた。
293.en: In little more than ten minutes, Konig, Grosser Kurfurst, Markgraf, Kaiser, Helgoland and others were hit. The German ships took more than thirty heavy shells. On the British side, only Colossus was hit, twice. Scheer was forced to turn away a third time.

297.ja: 反転を援護するため、シェーアは2つの命令を出す。まず19時13分、巡洋戦艦に命じた。「敵に突撃せよ。全力を尽くせ」。
297.en: To cover his battleships while they turned, he gave two orders. At 7:13 he sent the battlecruisers straight at the enemy, with the signal: "Battlecruisers, at the enemy! Give it everything!"

298.5.ja: リュッツォウはすでに大破して脱落し、ヒッパーは水雷艇で移乗先を探していた。残る4隻を率いたのはデアフリンガー艦長である。
298.5.en: By then Lutzow was too badly damaged to stay in the line. Hipper was in a torpedo boat, looking for a new flagship, and the other four battlecruisers were led by Derfflinger's captain.

299.2.ja: 4隻は集中砲火の中を数分間進み、デアフリンガーは後部砲塔2基を破壊され、その乗員はほぼ全滅した。
299.2.en: For several minutes the four ships steamed into the massed fire of the British line. Derfflinger's two after turrets were wrecked one after the other, and almost every man in them was killed.

300.ja: 2つ目は19時15分、水雷艇隊への突撃と煙幕の命令。19時18分、戦艦部隊は3度目の一斉回頭を終えて西へ退いた。
300.en: At 7:15 Scheer ordered the torpedo boats to attack and lay smoke. At 7:18 the battleships made their third battle turn-away, and withdrew to the west.

301.5.ja: 巡洋戦艦4隻も反転して離脱し、1隻も沈まなかった。ドイツでいう「死の騎行」だ。
301.5.en: The four battlecruisers then turned away themselves. None was sunk. The Germans called this charge the death ride.

309.ja: ドイツ水雷艇が放った魚雷は31本。ジェリコーはあらかじめ定めた対処法どおり、19時22分から2度に分けて、戦列を敵と反対側へ約45度回した。艦尾を魚雷に向けたのである。
309.en: The torpedo boats fired 31 torpedoes. Jellicoe answered as his battle orders laid down. From 7:22 he turned the battle line away in two steps, about 45 degrees in all, so that his ships' sterns faced the oncoming torpedoes.

310.6.ja: 走り終わりの魚雷は遅く、遠ざかる艦なら避けやすい。31本はすべて外れた。代わりに距離が開き、接触が切れた。
310.6.en: Near the end of its run a torpedo slows down, and a ship steaming away from it can dodge it easily. None of the 31 hit. The price was that the range opened, and the fleets lost touch.

311.5.ja: ジェリコーが針路を戻したとき、ドイツ艦隊は西へ十数キロの霧の中。日没まで1時間もなかった。
311.5.en: By the time Jellicoe turned back to his course, the Germans were more than five miles off to the west, in the haze, and sunset was less than an hour away.

313.ja: この転針は、ユトランド沖海戦で最も論争を呼んだ。批判者は言う。魚雷の来る方へ回っても避けられ、接触を保って日没までに大打撃を与えられた、と。
313.en: This turn-away is the most argued-over decision of the whole battle. Critics say that turning towards the torpedoes would have avoided them just as well, kept contact, and let the British land another heavy blow before sunset.

315.ja: 擁護する側は言う。離れる側へ回るのは、魚雷を確実にかわす定石の一つだった。ジェリコーの艦隊は、イギリスの海上優勢のすべてを担っていた。危険を冒さず有利な位置を守り、翌朝に戦うのは、彼の立場では理にかなっていた。
315.en: Jellicoe's defenders reply that turning away was one accepted answer to a torpedo attack, and a sure one. And his fleet was the whole foundation of British sea power. He had no need to gamble. Holding his strong position and fighting again at dawn made sense from where he stood.

316.5.ja: チャーチルは後に、ジェリコーを「午後のうちに戦争に負けうる、両軍でただ一人の男」と評した。
316.5.en: Winston Churchill later wrote that Jellicoe was the only man on either side who could lose the war in an afternoon.

321.ja: それから約1時間、両艦隊はほぼ並んで南西、さらに南へ進んだ。イギリスが東、ドイツが西。間の十数キロはもやに閉ざされ、互いに見えなかった。
321.en: For about the next hour, the two fleets steamed south-west, then south, on roughly parallel courses, the British to the east and the Germans to the west, with five miles or more of haze between them. Neither could see the other.

364.ja: 20時19分、先を行くビーティーの巡洋戦艦が、約9キロでドイツ巡洋戦艦と再び交戦した。ザイドリッツはまた被弾し、各艦とも撃てる主砲はわずかだった。
364.en: At 8:19, Beatty's battlecruisers, out ahead, found the German battlecruisers again, at about 10,000 yards. Seydlitz was hit several more times, and Hipper's ships had few big guns left in action.

368.5.ja: シェーアはマウヴェ少将の第2戦艦戦隊も連れていた。前弩級戦艦6隻で、最高18ノット。火力も防御も旧式で、全艦隊の動きを縛っていた。
368.5.en: Scheer had also brought along Rear-Admiral Franz Mauve's 2nd Battle Squadron: six pre-dreadnoughts, good for only 18 knots, and outclassed in both guns and armour. They held the whole fleet back.

369.ja: 近くにいたその戦隊が前に出て援護し、各艦が被弾したのち、西の闇へ退いた。20時35分ごろ砲声がやむ。これが主力艦同士の最後の砲火となった。
369.en: Now Mauve's squadron happened to be close by. It came forward to cover the battlecruisers, took hits of its own, then turned west into the dark. By about 8:35 the firing had stopped. It was the last time the big ships of the two fleets exchanged fire.

374.ja: 日没時、損害ではイギリスが不利だった。巡洋戦艦3隻と装甲巡洋艦1隻を失い、もう1隻の装甲巡洋艦も沈みかけ、戦死者は5千人近い。
374.en: At sunset the position stood like this. In losses, the British were worse off. They had lost three battlecruisers and an armoured cruiser, a second armoured cruiser was sinking, and nearly 5,000 men were dead.

376.5.ja: ドイツは主力艦をまだ失っていないが、リュッツォウはもう救えず、ザイドリッツとデアフリンガーは大破、第3戦艦戦隊の先頭の艦も傷ついていた。
376.5.en: The Germans had not yet lost a capital ship. But Lutzow could not be saved, Seydlitz and Derfflinger were badly damaged, and the leading ships of the 3rd Battle Squadron had all been hit.

378.ja: だが位置ではドイツが不利だった。グランド・フリートが南東、大洋艦隊が北西。ジェリコーはシェーアの帰路をふさぎ、その戦艦24隻はほぼ無傷だった。
378.en: In position, though, the Germans were worse off. The Grand Fleet lay to the south-east, the High Seas Fleet to the north-west. Jellicoe was across Scheer's road home, and his 24 battleships were almost untouched.

380.ja: この時期、この海域の昼は17時間ほど。夜明けにこの位置のままなら、ドイツ艦隊が逃げ切るのは難しい。夜の問題はただ1つ、シェーアが夜明け前にイギリス艦隊を回り込むか、突き抜けられるかだった。
380.en: In those waters, at that time of year, there were about seventeen hours of daylight. If the fleets were still placed like this at dawn, the Germans would find it very hard to escape a second time. So the night came down to one question: could Scheer get round the British fleet, or through it, before daybreak?

386.ja: ジェリコーは夜の主力決戦を求めないと決めた。グランド・フリートは夜戦訓練が乏しく、探照灯の扱いも夜間射撃もドイツに劣る。闇では敵味方の区別がつきにくく、主力艦が入り乱れれば水雷艇の餌食になり、数の優位も生きない。
386.en: Jellicoe decided not to seek a battle in the dark. The Grand Fleet had never trained seriously for night fighting, and its searchlight work and night gunnery were worse than the Germans'. At night it was hard to tell friend from foe. And big ships tangled up at close range in the dark were easy prey for torpedo boats, with no way to use his advantage in numbers.

390.ja: 21時ごろ、彼は戦艦部隊を間隔の狭い数列の縦隊にまとめ、17ノットで南下させた。駆逐艦隊は5海里後ろに置き、後衛を兼ねて、近づく敵を襲わせた。
390.en: At about 9 p.m. he ordered the battle fleet into closer columns, heading south at 17 knots. His destroyer flotillas were stationed five miles astern, as a rearguard, ready to attack anything that came near.

392.ja: ジェリコーは、シェーアの帰り道を読まねばならない。最短は南東のホーンズ・リーフを回り、ユトランド半島の西岸を南下する道。次はヘルゴラント島の西を南下する道。最も遠いのは南西のエムス河口を経る道だ。
392.en: Jellicoe had to guess Scheer's route home. There were several channels through the minefields. The shortest ran south-east to Horns Reef, then down the coast of Jutland. The next passed west of Heligoland. The longest went south-west, to the mouth of the Ems.

394.5.ja: ジェリコーはシェーアが南へ向かうと読み、艦隊を南に置いた。ホーンズ・リーフ方面には、機雷敷設艦アブディールに機雷を足させただけだった。
394.5.en: Jellicoe judged that Scheer would head south, and placed his fleet to the south. To cover Horns Reef, he sent only the minelayer Abdiel, to lay more mines there.

398.ja: シェーアが選んだのは、そのホーンズ・リーフだった。21時14分、全艦隊に南南東、16ノットでの帰投を命じ、何があっても針路を保てと指示する。飛行船には夜明けのホーンズ・リーフ偵察を求めた。
398.en: In fact Scheer chose Horns Reef. At 9:14 he ordered the whole fleet home, course south-south-east, 16 knots, and told every ship to hold that course whatever happened. He also asked for airships to scout off Horns Reef at dawn.

399.6.ja: ほかに道はなかった。遠回りすれば夜明けにまだイギリス艦隊の近くにいる。最短の道をとってこそ、明るくなる前に自国の機雷原の内側へ入れる見込みがあった。
399.6.en: He had no real choice. By any of the longer routes, he would still be close to the British at daybreak. Only the shortest gave him a chance of getting behind his own minefields before dawn.

402.ja: こうして両艦隊の航路は夜の海で交わる。やや速いグランド・フリートは南へ進んで前に出ており、南東へ向かう大洋艦隊はその航跡を斜めに横切った。出会ったのは、後方に置かれたイギリス駆逐艦隊だった。
402.en: So during the night the two fleets' tracks crossed. The Grand Fleet, heading south, was a little faster and out in front. The High Seas Fleet, heading south-east, cut across behind it, and ran into the British destroyer flotillas stationed astern.

404.5.ja: ヒッパーがモルトケに移り、偵察部隊の指揮を取り戻したのは21時過ぎだった。
404.5.en: Only after 9 p.m. did Hipper get aboard Moltke and take back command of his scouting forces.

450.ja: 40号室はこの夜、シェーアの帰投命令の針路と速力も、飛行船にホーンズ・リーフ偵察を求めた電報も解読していた。海軍省は23時ごろ針路と速力をジェリコーに伝えたが、偵察要請など重要な電報数通は回さなかった。
450.en: That night Room 40 intercepted and decoded Scheer's order to head home, with his course and speed. It also picked up his request for airships over Horns Reef. At about 11 p.m. the Admiralty passed the course and speed to Jellicoe. But the airship request, and several other key signals, were never sent on.

456.ja: その針路を海図に延ばせば、ホーンズ・リーフに行き着く。だが海軍省は昼にシェーアの旗艦位置を誤報し、夜にも明らかにおかしな位置を伝えていた。ジェリコーはこの電報を信じなかった。
456.en: Plotted on a chart, the course Jellicoe was given led straight to Horns Reef. But the Admiralty had already misplaced Scheer's flagship at midday, and after dark it had sent him a German position that was plainly wrong. So Jellicoe did not trust this one.

484.ja: 22時から翌2時ごろまで、接触は七、八回。経過はどれも似ている。数百から2千メートルで出会うが、敵か味方か分からない。ドイツ艦が識別信号で探り、すぐ探照灯をつけて副砲を斉射する。数分で明かりが消え、海は闇に戻る。
484.en: Between 10 p.m. and about 2 a.m. there were seven or eight clashes, and most went the same way. Ships sighted each other at anything from a few hundred yards to a mile or so, and neither side could be sure the other was hostile. The Germans flashed their recognition signal, then switched on searchlights and opened fire with their secondary guns. A few minutes later the searchlights went out, and the sea was dark again.

486.ja: 22時15分ごろ、グッドイナフの第2軽巡洋艦戦隊とドイツ第4偵察群が、千メートル足らずで撃ち合った。
486.en: The main clashes went like this. At about 10:15, Goodenough's 2nd Light Cruiser Squadron fought the German 4th Scouting Group at less than a thousand yards.

489.ja: サウサンプトンは89人が死傷したが、その放った魚雷1本がドイツ軽巡洋艦フラウエンロープを沈めた。320人が戦死し、生存者は9人だった。
489.en: Southampton had 89 casualties. But a torpedo she fired sank the German light cruiser Frauenlob. Frauenlob lost 320 men; only nine survived.

530.ja: 23時ごろ、イギリス第4駆逐艦隊は右舷に大型艦の列を見つけた。味方かと発光信号で問うと、返ってきたのは探照灯と砲火。ドイツ戦列の先頭、第1戦艦戦隊のヴェストファーレンやナッサウだった。
530.en: At about 11 p.m., the British 4th Destroyer Flotilla saw a line of big ships to starboard. Thinking they might be friendly, they flashed a challenge. The answer was searchlights and gunfire. It was the head of the German battle line: Westfalen, Nassau and other ships of the 1st Battle Squadron.

537.5.ja: 隊を率いるティペラリーは数分で炎上し、のちに沈没。駆逐艦スピットファイアはナッサウと衝突して大破したが、自力で帰った。
537.5.en: The flotilla leader Tipperary was ablaze within minutes, and later sank. The destroyer Spitfire collided with Nassau. Badly damaged, she still got home under her own steam.

546.ja: イギリス戦列の最後尾、第5戦艦戦隊は後方の砲火を見ていた。マラヤではドイツ弩級艦の輪郭を見分けた者もいたが、艦長は、旗艦にも見えているはずで、命令なく撃って位置を明かすべきでないと考え、撃ちも報告もしなかった。
546.en: The 5th Battle Squadron, at the tail of the British line, could see the firing astern. In Malaya, someone recognised the outline of a German dreadnought. But her captain assumed his flagship could see it too, and that without orders he should not open fire and give his position away. He neither fired nor reported.

555.ja: ドイツ軽巡洋艦の何隻かは魚雷を避けて味方戦艦の列を突っ切り、エルビングは戦艦ポーゼンに衝突されて機関室が浸水、動けなくなった。ロストックは魚雷を受けた。
555.en: Dodging torpedoes, several German light cruisers cut through their own battle line. Elbing was rammed by the battleship Posen, her engine rooms flooded, and she lost power. Rostock was hit by a torpedo.

556.ja: 2隻とも翌朝、自沈処分された。
556.en: Both were scuttled by their own side the next morning.

563.ja: 単独で帰るモルトケとザイドリッツを見たイギリス戦艦もあったが、やはり撃たず、報告もしなかった。
563.en: Several other British battleships sighted the German battlecruisers Moltke and Seydlitz, making their own way home. They too neither fired nor reported.

584.5.ja: 真夜中前後、駆逐艦フォーチュンとアーデントが沈んだ。ブロークは被弾で舵がきかなくなり、味方のスパローホークに衝突。スパローホークは翌朝、味方の手で沈められた。
584.5.en: Around midnight, the British destroyers Fortune and Ardent were sunk, one after the other. The flotilla leader Broke, her steering wrecked by a hit, rammed the destroyer Sparrowhawk, which the British themselves had to sink the next morning.

594.5.ja: 装甲巡洋艦ブラック・プリンスは夕方から本隊とはぐれ、0時10分ごろドイツ戦列を味方と誤って近づいた。至近距離から戦艦数隻に撃たれて爆沈し、857人全員が戦死した。
594.5.en: The armoured cruiser Black Prince had lost touch with her squadron that evening. At about ten past midnight she mistook the German battle line for friendly ships and closed in. Several battleships opened fire at point-blank range. She blew up and sank, with all 857 men aboard.

612.5.ja: 駆逐艦タービュレントも、ドイツ戦列の前で沈んだ。
612.5.en: A little later, the destroyer Turbulent was also sunk, ahead of the German line.

616.ja: こうして大洋艦隊は2、3時間で、グランド・フリート主力の数海里後ろを抜けた。
616.en: And so, over two or three hours, the High Seas Fleet slipped past a few miles astern of the Grand Fleet.

618.ja: ジェリコーが知らなかった理由は4つある。目撃艦が報告しなかったこと、駆逐艦の報告が届かなかったこと、ジェリコー自身の判断、そして海軍省の情報が生かされなかったことだ。
618.en: Jellicoe never found out, for four reasons. The men who saw the Germans did not report. The destroyers' reports never reached him. His own judgement played a part. And the Admiralty's intelligence was not put to proper use.

620.ja: ジェリコーも旗艦アイアン・デュークの乗員も、後方の砲声と閃光に気づいていたが、味方駆逐艦とドイツ軽艦艇の予想どおりの戦闘だと考えた。
620.en: He and his staff on the flagship, Iron Duke, could hear the firing astern and see the flashes. But they took it for their own destroyers fighting German light forces, which was just what they expected.

622.ja: 多くの駆逐艦は無線機を壊されていた。他艦が報告したと思った艦長もいれば、最後まで相手がドイツ主力だと知らなかった艦もある。
622.en: Many destroyers' wireless sets had been shot away. Some captains assumed someone else had reported. Some did not realise until after the battle that they had met the German battle fleet.

624.ja: 4つとも、根っこは同じだ。イギリス艦隊には上の命令を待つ習慣が染みつき、下の指揮官は、見たことを報告するのが自分の務めだと考えなかった。この集中した指揮は昼には艦隊を整然と動かしたが、夜には弱点になった。
624.en: All four had one root. The British fleet had long been in the habit of waiting for orders from above, and junior officers who saw something did not think reporting it was their job. By day, that tightly centralised command kept the fleet moving as one. At night, it was a weakness.

651.5.ja: 同じころ、深手のドイツ艦が次々に沈んだ。リュッツォウは主砲弾約24発を受け、約8千トン浸水。艦首は沈み、スクリューが水面に出て、もう進めなかった。
651.5.en: During those same hours, several badly damaged German ships went down. Lutzow had taken about 24 heavy shells and some 8,000 tons of water. Her bow was under, her propellers were out of the water, and she could no longer steam.

686.ja: ヴィースバーデンは両軍の間で一晩漂ったのち明け方に沈み、生存者は1人だけだった。
686.en: Wiesbaden drifted between the fleets all night, and sank in the early hours. Only one of her crew survived.

689.8.ja: 艦長は総員退艦を命じ、千人あまりが水雷艇に移った。1時45分、水雷艇G38が魚雷でリュッツォウを沈めた。
689.8.en: Her captain ordered her abandoned. More than a thousand men were taken off by the escorting torpedo boats, and at 1:45 a.m. the torpedo boat G38 sank her with torpedoes.

705.ja: 2時ごろ、空が白み始めた。イギリス第12駆逐艦隊が、旗艦フォークナーに率いられてドイツ艦隊の後尾を発見した。目標がはっきり見えたこの攻撃は、夜を通じて最も効果をあげた雷撃となった。
705.en: At about 2 a.m. it began to grow light. The British 12th Destroyer Flotilla, led by Faulknor, sighted the rear of the German fleet. They attacked in the dawn light, with the targets clear to see. It was the most effective torpedo attack of the night.

715.ja: 2時10分、魚雷が前弩級戦艦ポンメルンに命中して弾薬庫が誘爆し、船体は折れて沈んだ。839人全員が戦死。この海戦でドイツが失った唯一の戦艦である。
715.en: At 2:10, a torpedo hit the pre-dreadnought Pommern and set off a magazine. She broke apart and sank, and all 839 men aboard were killed. She was the only battleship the Germans lost in the battle.

717.ja: フォークナーは発見したドイツ戦艦の位置と針路を3度報告したが、アイアン・デュークには1通も届かなかった。ドイツの妨害電波のせいかもしれない。
717.en: Faulknor sent three reports giving the German battleships' position and course. Iron Duke received none of them, perhaps because of German jamming.

718.7.ja: ザイドリッツは主砲弾21発と魚雷1本を受けて約5300トン浸水し、低速で単独帰投する途中、ホーンズ・リーフ付近で2度座礁した。港へ曳航されたのは6月2日朝だった。
718.7.en: Seydlitz had taken 21 heavy shells and a torpedo, and had some 5,300 tons of water aboard. She crept home alone, ran aground twice near Horns Reef, and was not towed into harbour until the morning of 2 June.

720.ja: ジェリコーはホーンズ・リーフの南西約30海里にいた。夜の混乱で艦隊は散らばっていた。北へ転じて戦力を集めつつ敵を探したが、ドイツ艦の姿はなかった。
720.en: Jellicoe was now about 30 miles south-west of Horns Reef, his fleet scattered by the confusion of the night. He turned north, gathering his ships and searching for the enemy. But there was no German ship in sight.

721.ja: 3時ごろ、大洋艦隊の先頭はホーンズ・リーフに達し、自国の機雷原の内側に入った。
721.en: At about 3 a.m., the head of the High Seas Fleet reached Horns Reef and entered the channel behind its own minefields.

722.2.ja: 4時15分、海軍省から、ドイツ艦隊がホーンズ・リーフに迫ったとの報が届く。もう追撃はできない。グランド・フリートは午前中に帰途についた。
722.2.en: At 4:15, the Admiralty told Jellicoe that the German fleet was nearing Horns Reef. It was too late to catch them. That morning the Grand Fleet turned for home.

722.6.ja: 5時20分、帰投中の戦艦オストフリースラントが、前夜アブディールの敷いた機雷に触れたが、沈まなかった。
722.6.en: On the way into port, at 5:20, the battleship Ostfriesland struck one of Abdiel's mines. She was damaged, but did not sink.

723.ja: イギリスの沈没は14隻、約11万3300トン。戦死6094人、負傷674人、捕虜177人。
723.en: The British lost 14 ships, about 113,300 tons. 6,094 men were killed, 674 wounded and 177 taken prisoner.

723.4.ja: ドイツは11隻、約6万2300トン。戦死2551人、負傷507人。
723.4.en: The Germans lost 11 ships, about 62,300 tons, with 2,551 killed and 507 wounded.

723.8.ja: イギリスは巡洋戦艦3隻、インディファティガブル、クイーン・メアリー、インヴィンシブル。装甲巡洋艦3隻、ディフェンス、ウォリアー、ブラック・プリンス。駆逐艦8隻、ティペラリー、シャーク、スパローホーク、タービュレント、アーデント、フォーチュン、ノーマッド、ネスター。
723.8.en: The British losses: three battlecruisers, Indefatigable, Queen Mary and Invincible; three armoured cruisers, Defence, Warrior and Black Prince; and eight destroyers, Tipperary, Shark, Sparrowhawk, Turbulent, Ardent, Fortune, Nomad and Nestor.

724.2.ja: ドイツは巡洋戦艦リュッツォウ、前弩級戦艦ポンメルン、軽巡洋艦4隻、ヴィースバーデン、エルビング、ロストック、フラウエンロープ、水雷艇5隻、V4、V27、V29、V48、S35。
724.2.en: The German losses: one battlecruiser, Lutzow; one pre-dreadnought, Pommern; four light cruisers, Wiesbaden, Elbing, Rostock and Frauenlob; and five torpedo boats, V4, V27, V29, V48 and S35.

724.6.ja: 砲術では、通説の集計で、イギリス主力艦は主砲弾4534発を撃って123発命中、約2.7パーセント。ドイツは3597発で124発、約3.4パーセントだった。
724.6.en: As for gunnery, by the usual count the British capital ships fired 4,534 heavy shells and scored 123 hits, about 2.7 per cent. The Germans fired 3,597 and scored 124, about 3.4 per cent.

725.ja: 勝敗には物差しが要る。損害で測ればドイツが優位だ。沈んだトン数はイギリスの半分強、戦死者は半分以下。ドイツは当時、これを根拠に勝利を宣言した。
725.en: Who won depends on how you measure it. On losses, Germany came out ahead. It lost little more than half the British tonnage, and fewer than half as many men. The German government claimed a victory at once, on exactly that basis.

725.4.ja: 戦後の海の情勢で測ればイギリスが優位だ。スカパ・フローに戻ったジェリコーは6月2日夜、戦艦部隊は補給を終え、4時間で再出撃できると報告した。
725.4.en: On the state of things at sea afterwards, Britain came out ahead. Back at Scapa Flow on the evening of 2 June, Jellicoe reported the battle fleet refuelled, re-armed and ready to sail at four hours' notice.

725.7.ja: ドイツの巡洋戦艦数隻は、修理に3か月から4か月あまりかかった。封鎖は1日も途切れなかった。
725.7.en: Several German battlecruisers spent three or four months under repair. The blockade was never lifted for a single day.

726.ja: 大洋艦隊はグランド・フリートを削って戦力差を縮めようとしたが、果たせなかった。イギリスは巡洋戦艦3隻を失ったが、弩級戦艦の数の差は変わらず、1か月後には使える戦力が戦前を上回った。
726.en: The High Seas Fleet had sailed to whittle down the Grand Fleet and shift the balance of strength. It failed. Britain lost three battlecruisers, but the count of dreadnought battleships did not change, and within a month the Grand Fleet had more ships ready for action than before the battle.

726.3.ja: 作戦の狙いで測れば、どちらも果たせていない。ドイツは敵の一部をたたき、主力は避けるはずだった。それが主力に出くわし、3度の一斉回頭と夜の突破でようやく逃れた。
726.3.en: Measured by what each side set out to do, neither succeeded. The Germans had meant to destroy part of the British fleet and avoid its main body. Instead they ran into the main body, and escaped only by three battle turn-aways and a breakthrough at night.

726.6.ja: イギリスは大洋艦隊の撃滅を狙い、2度有利な位置を占めながら戦果を広げられず、夜には敵の退路をふさぐ位置も手放した。
726.6.en: The British had meant to destroy the High Seas Fleet. Twice they won the better position and could not make it count, and in the night they lost the intercepting position they already held.

726.9.ja: アメリカの新聞は評した。「ドイツ艦隊は看守を襲ったが、まだ牢の中にいる」。最も雄弁なのは、ドイツ自身の結論である。
726.9.en: An American newspaper summed it up at the time: the German fleet had assaulted its jailer, but it was still in jail. The Germans' own conclusion says even more.

727.2.ja: 1916年7月4日、シェーアは皇帝に報告した。艦隊決戦で最善の結果を得ても、イギリスは講和に応じない。近いうちにイギリスを倒せるのは、海上貿易をねらう潜水艦戦だけだ、と。
727.2.en: On 4 July 1916, Scheer reported to the Kaiser that even the most successful fleet battle could not force Britain to make peace. The only way to defeat Britain within a reasonable time was a submarine war on her trade.

727.5.ja: 大洋艦隊はその後、1916年8月と10月、1918年4月に出撃したが、イギリス主力艦とは戦わなかった。ドイツは1917年2月1日に無制限潜水艦作戦を再開し、4月6日にはアメリカが対独宣戦。ユトランド沖海戦は海の戦力比を変えなかったが、ドイツの戦争指導を変えさせた。
727.5.en: The High Seas Fleet came out three more times, in August and October 1916 and in April 1918, and never again fought the British capital ships. On 1 February 1917 Germany resumed unrestricted submarine warfare, and on 6 April the United States declared war on Germany. In that sense Jutland left the balance at sea where it was, but it helped turn German strategy towards the U-boat.

727.9.ja: イギリスの損害が大きかった原因は、主に自分の側にあった。巡洋戦艦3隻は、どれも砲塔の被弾から炎が弾薬庫へ回って爆沈した。主因は装薬の扱いで、装甲の薄さはその次だ。同じ被弾で爆沈したドイツ艦はない。
727.9.en: Why did the British lose so much more? Mostly because of their own failings. All three battlecruisers blew up after a hit on a turret let fire through to the magazine. The main cause was the way they handled cordite, more than their thin armour. German ships took hits of the same kind, and not one blew up.

728.15.ja: 弱点は双方にある。イギリスは4つ。第一に、巡洋戦艦の防御の薄さ。
728.15.en: Each side had weaknesses of its own. The British had four. The first: the battlecruisers were thinly armoured.

728.25.ja: この艦種はフィッシャー第一海軍卿の構想で、戦艦なみの主砲と高速の代わりに装甲を削った。本来は偵察や敵巡洋艦の追撃に使う艦で、敵主力と戦列を組んで撃ち合うためのものではなかった。
728.25.en: The type was the brainchild of Admiral Sir John Fisher, as First Sea Lord: battleship guns and more speed, paid for with less armour. Battlecruisers were meant to scout and to hunt down enemy cruisers, not to stand in the line against enemy capital ships.

728.4.ja: 第二に、装薬の扱いが緩かった。ドッガー・バンクのあと、イギリスの巡洋戦艦部隊は発射速度を上げようと、砲塔や揚弾の通路に装薬を置き、防火扉を開け放つのが常だった。砲塔が燃えれば、炎は通路伝いに弾薬庫へ届く。
728.4.en: The second: careless handling of cordite. After Dogger Bank, to raise their rate of fire, the battlecruiser crews took to keeping charges ready in the turrets and hoists, with the flash doors left open. So once a turret was hit and set alight, the flash could run straight down the hoist to the magazine.

728.55.ja: 第三に、徹甲弾の出来が悪く、当たっても貫けなかった。リュッツォウ、デアフリンガー、ザイドリッツは主砲弾を20発前後ずつ受けたが、リュッツォウ以外は帰港した。
728.55.en: The third: British armour-piercing shells were poor. They hit, but did not go through. Lutzow, Derfflinger and Seydlitz each took around twenty heavy shells, and all but Lutzow got home.

728.65.ja: 厚い装甲に斜めに当たると、貫く前に砕けたり、早く炸裂したりしたのである。
728.65.en: Striking thick armour at an angle, the shells often broke up, or burst before they got through.

728.75.ja: 第四に、通信と報告の仕組みの欠陥。午後には第5戦艦戦隊が2度転針に遅れ、夕方にはジェリコーが展開前に敵の方位を知らず、夜にはドイツ艦隊が後ろを抜けても報告がなかった。3つとも同じ性質の問題だ。
728.75.en: The fourth: signalling and reporting. In the afternoon, the 5th Battle Squadron twice failed to turn with Beatty in time. In the evening, Jellicoe had to deploy without knowing where the enemy was. At night, the German fleet crossed astern and nobody told him. All three were the same failure.

728.9.ja: ドイツの強みは訓練とダメージ・コントロールだ。砲戦初めの測距、一斉回頭、夜戦、傷ついた艦を沈めない手際で、イギリスにまさった。
728.9.en: The Germans' strengths were training and damage control. Their early ranging, their battle turn-aways, their night fighting, and their saving of crippled ships were all better than the British.

729.ja: 弱みは偵察だった。シェーアは1日に2度、敵情を知らないまま艦隊をイギリス戦列の集中砲火へ進めた。逃れられたのは訓練のおかげであり、もやと日没のおかげでもあった。
729.en: Their weakness was scouting. Twice in one day Scheer led his fleet blind into the massed fire of the British line. He got away partly through good training, and partly thanks to the haze and the sunset.

729.15.ja: だが根本は動かない。弩級戦艦16隻対28隻。大洋艦隊が正面の決戦で勝つことはできなかった。
729.15.en: But none of this changes the basic fact. With 16 dreadnoughts against 28, the High Seas Fleet could never win a stand-up fight with the Grand Fleet.
